question: A 3580-g (7-lb 14-oz) male newborn is delivered at 36 weeks' gestation to a 26-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1 after an uncomplicated pregnancy. His temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), heart rate is 96/min, and respirations are 55/min and irregular. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 65% measured in the right hand. He sneezes and grimaces during suction of secretions from his mouth. There is some flexion movement. The trunk is pink and the extremities are blue. The cord is clamped and the newborn is dried and wrapped in a prewarmed towel. Which of the following is the most appropriate next best step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Blue extremities suggest poor oxygenation -> Low oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry -> Possible respiratory distress -> 70%
enhanced_information: The newborn's blue extremities suggest poor oxygenation, confirmed by low oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry, indicating possible respiratory distress. The most appropriate next step would be to administer positive pressure ventilation to improve oxygenation and support the newborn's respiratory function.
analysis: The newborn is showing signs of respiratory distress with poor oxygenation, indicated by the low oxygen saturation and blue extremities. Administering positive pressure ventilation is the most appropriate next step to improve oxygenation and support respiratory function in this scenario.
